title: FDA Adverse Event Signals FAERS
description:
Queries the openFDA Drug Adverse Event Reporting System for the most recent 30 days of available data, counting serious adverse events and death reports by drug name. Computes a death percentage and assigns severity tiers (CRITICAL >= 10%, HIGH >= 5%, ELEVATED >= 1%). A sudden spike in serious event count for a specific drug - especially with rising death reports - is a leading indicator of black box warnings, label changes, or outright recalls. Trending this data over time with streamstats reveals statistical anomalies weeks before FDA action moves pharma stocks 30-70%. No API key required.

Note: openFDA's adverse-event dataset updates quarterly with a multi-month lag (the dataset is typically 90-150 days behind real-time). The script anchors its 30-day window to the API's `last_updated` field rather than today's date so it always returns data that exists. The output includes a `data_age_days` column so downstream readers can see how stale the signal is and decide whether to act on it.
